visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 consistently places the projectile path, velocity components, flight-time marker, and range line correctly from launch to landing, whereas Lesson 2 is mostly correct but its horizontal-range diagram shows the range arrow stopping well short of the landing point and has a less positionally faithful projectile marker.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 1 includes a functional fill-in gate with a real prompt, correct answer, hint, remediation path, and matching plan wiring after act_introduction, whereas Lesson 2 has no gate specs or plan JSON at all, so it provides no verifiable interactivity.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 2’s narration is mostly clear and correctly spoken despite being a bit dense, while Lesson 1 includes a confusing spoken defect where it describes the range as “thirty-four point six meters per second for just over four seconds,” using the wrong quantity/unit before later giving a different final answer.

sync.rationale: Lesson 1 provides multiple timed cues that generally coincide with the narration's references to vectors, trajectory, vertical focus, horizontal focus, and final range despite some missing/early formula-related cues, whereas Lesson 2 has no beat/timing data or triggered visual cues at all, making synchronization unverifiable and effectively worse for this dimension.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 is equally mathematically correct but builds the concept more pedagogically by visualizing decomposition, separately analyzing vertical time and horizontal range, and explicitly framing time as the bridge, whereas Lesson 2 gives the right formulas and numbers but is more compressed and mostly states the flight-time formula without much derivational support.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 has large, legible text, clean slide layouts, consistent bright styling, and well-spaced diagrams, whereas Lesson 1 is frequently pushed into the left half with large empty space, uses tiny hard-to-read labels and dim text boxes, and feels cluttered by persistent UI/controls.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 1 is the clear overall winner: four of six agents favored it, including high-confidence wins in interactivity, synchronization, visual accuracy, and concept accuracy. Its strongest advantages are that it has verified interactive gating, timed visual cues aligned to narration, more positionally accurate projectile diagrams, and a more pedagogically complete treatment of vertical time and horizontal range. Lesson 2 was preferred for narration quality and polish, with especially strong polish, but those strengths do not outweigh Lesson 1’s broader and higher-confidence advantages across instructional functionality, synchronization, and conceptual presentation.
